script.title: Why a Town's Gas Station Fuel Hit 172 Degrees
sentences: In 1979, a gas station owner's fuel dipstick came out hot.
This was Centralia, a Pennsylvania coal town of about a thousand people.
He lowered a thermometer into his underground tank on a string.
Two years later, a hole 150 feet deep opened under a 12-year-old boy in his grandmother's backyard.
He held onto a tree root until his cousin pulled him out.
A fire had been burning in the abandoned coal mines under the town since at least 1962.
At its current rate, it could keep burning for over 250 years.
script.description:
A Pennsylvania town has had a coal fire under it since 1962.
It started showing up in a gas tank.
claims_en: In 1979, a gas-station owner in Centralia found his dipstick was hot after checking an underground tank.
Centralia is a coal (anthracite) mining borough in Pennsylvania; it had 1,012 residents in 1980.
He lowered a thermometer into the tank on a string.
The gasoline in the tank was 172 °F.
On February 14, 1981, a 12-year-old fell into a sinkhole 150 feet deep that opened in his grandmother's backyard; he grabbed a tree root and his cousin pulled him out.
The steam from the hole contained a lethal level of carbon monoxide.
A coal-seam fire has been burning in the abandoned mines under Centralia since at least May 27, 1962.
At its current rate the fire could continue to burn for over 250 years.
